title: Simon the magician (Acts 8:4–25)
hookLine: a man who has already believed reaches for his purse. why?
tomorrow: why would a queen's treasurer need help reading?

cards: A front-row seat, a skip-the-line pass, a bigger following: plenty of things can be bought. Today's story has a man who tries to buy something that can't.
After Stephen's death the believers scatter, and Philip, one of the seven, goes down to a city of Samaria. Crowds listen, and "there was great joy in that city."
But one man there already has a following: Simon, who had "used sorcery, and bewitched the people of Samaria." Here's the strange part. Simon isn't an enemy.
"Then Simon himself believed also: and when he was baptized, he continued with Philip." So why, a few verses later, is a brand-new believer reaching for his money?

teach.b: Word reaches Jerusalem, and Peter and John come down. They pray for the new believers and lay hands on them, and they receive the Holy Ghost. Simon watches, and sees what looks to him like a technique.
So he brings money: "Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost." That's the answer to the puzzle.
Simon believed, but he still thought like his old trade: power is something a professional acquires, for a fee. He brought the marketplace into the church with him, without noticing.

teach.h: THE GIFT OF GOD, NOT FOR SALE.
teach.b: Peter's reply is fierce: "Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money." The key word is gift. A gift can be received, thanked for, passed along.

The moment it's bought, it stops being a gift. Something to tell a friend tonight: it's the same word Peter used at Pentecost, when he promised the crowd, "ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost."
Free then, free now. Peter doesn't leave it at a rebuke, though. He tells Simon to repent and pray, "if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee."

teach.h: PRAY YE TO THE LORD FOR ME.
teach.b: And Simon's last words in the story are a request: "Pray ye to the Lord for me."
Acts never says what became of him.

how: Christians speak of grace as God's free gift, and the laws of some churches forbid buying or selling sacraments or church offices.

o: a fortune-teller Paul silenced in Philippi
a court wizard who opposed Moses in Egypt
a Samaritan who tried to buy the Spirit's power

games.q: who did what in Samaria — tap the pairs.
p: preached in a city of Samaria

s: Acts says Simon himself believed also, was baptized and stayed with Philip. the trouble came after.
Peter cursed Simon and left him no way back
Peter told him to repent and pray, if perhaps the thought of his heart might be forgiven.
Peter called the Spirit the gift of God
the same word he used at Pentecost: ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.

games.q: a friend with a big exam tomorrow offers you twenty dollars to pray for her. what fits Peter's answer to Simon?
o: pray for her gladly, and turn down the money.
take it; Simon's problem was the amount, not the money.
don't pray at all, since money was offered.
games.why: Peter's objection was the idea that the gift of God may be purchased with money. prayer stays a gift: given freely, never sold.

practice: Count three good things in your life you didn't earn, one finger at a time: a person, a morning, a second chance. With each one, notice any urge to pay it back or prove you deserve it, and set that urge down.
Let all three stay gifts, with no price on them.

wordCard.voice: Simon the magician. A man of Samaria who believed, then tried to buy the power to give the Holy Ghost.

orig.note: Greek: gift, a free gift; Peter's word in Acts 8:20, the gift of God.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: not for sale, because a gift that's bought stops being a gift. See you tomorrow.
